title: cross-thread-synthesis-1on1-prep-uma-2026-07-03
content:
Meeting: cross-thread synthesis 1:1 (Product <> Eng <> Applied ML)
Date: 2026-07-06 10:00am PT (prep notes)
Owner: Uma Patel
Goal: align on prioritized roadmap bets for H2 (dedicated capacity, KV-cache improvements, and prompt-eval automation). Surface risks, quick win list, and agree on measurable signals to decide go/no-go for Q3 spikes.

Context / what I need from this 1:1
- Quick sync to reduce ambiguity before xfunc roadmap review on 7/10.
- Confirm eng capacity for two medium-sized spikes (KV cache partial rollouts + token-savings batching).
- Get Research commitment on evaluation plan for cache regression tests and promptset coverage.
- Lock on metrics and SLAs that Product will use in customer-communication drafts.

Attendees (proposed)
- Lena Cho (PM, Product - Hosted API)
- Marcus Reid (Staff SWE, Serving Runtime)
- Diego Morales (Applied ML, evaluation and dataset ownership)
- Uma Patel (note-taker / program lead)

Agenda (25-30m total)
1) 3m context & desired outcome from Product (Lena)
2) 6m brief from Eng: what’s feasible in next 8 weeks, blockers, infra deps (Marcus)
3) 6m applied-ml: eval plan outline, datasets, regression signals (Diego)
4) 6m align on metrics, release gating criteria, and owner assignments
5) 4m next steps + calendar/PRIO decisions

Background summary (short)
- Product: customers asking for 20-40% token-cost savings on common chat workloads and better predictable p95 latency under bursty traffic. They want a plan that doesn’t regress quality.
- Eng: kernel-level batching and KV-cache path has a prototype, but needs integration testing and canary infra. Risk: partial cache invalidation logic for multi-tenant scenarios.
- Research: we have an eval harness but it lacks representative prompt sets for PLG customers; need to expand and add end-to-end latency-aware metrics.

Key discussion prompts (prep notes for me)
- What latency delta is acceptable for Product if we gain 30% token cost reduction? (proposal: <= +5% p95 latency during steady-state)
- Can Eng ship a narrow canary that targets only <=10% of traffic in 6 weeks? If not, what minimal scope?
- What are the top 3 prompt archetypes we must include in cache-regression tests? (Customer-facing chat, code-completion snippets, short transactional queries)
- How will we measure "quality regressions"? (suggestion: BLEU not enough — use combined automatic checks + a small blind human eval sample for anchor prompts)

Risk register (to raise quickly)
- Multi-tenant KV invalidation bug could surface silently and cause stale outputs — critical. Need rollback and telemetry hooks.
- Batching change may increase tail latency in worst-case bursts (spiky traffic) — need load-testing with synthetic traces resembling top 5 customers.
- Eval coverage gap: current prompt sets biased to internal tests; may miss PLG edge cases.

Proposed decision slate (what we need to decide in the meeting)
- Approve 6-week canary for KV caching with scope: only models x, y (quantized), and traffic subset A (10% of hosted tier). Owner: Marcus.
- Approve Research to expand promptset by EOD 7/13 and deliver a prioritized list of 50 anchor prompts. Owner: Diego.
- Product to draft public messaging guardrails and internal “customer comms” template by 7/17. Owner: Lena.

Concrete metrics / gating (strings to capture now)
- Safety net: if quality metric (human eval anchor score) drops >3 absolute points on any anchor prompt cohort -> automatic rollback and pause.
- Latency SLO: steady-state p95 increase must be <= +5% vs baseline for traffic subset during canary. If >+10% -> rollback.
- Cost target: token-unit cost reduction >= 20% across canonical chat workload during canary window.
- Observability: must ship a dashboard with model-level per-route p50/p95, token-count changes, and cache-hit-rate by 7/13. Owner: Eng/Observability.

Action items (assigned)
- Marcus: prepare canary implementation plan + list of infra risks + rollback plan. Due: 2026-07-10. (JIRA-2034)
- Diego: expand promptset, add PLG samples, and define auto-eval threshold scripts. Deliver prioritized anchor list. Due: 2026-07-13.
- Lena: draft external/internal comms templates and decision memo for leadership. Due: 2026-07-17.
- Uma: schedule xfunc review slot (7/10) and circulate this note + short TL;DR. Due: 2026-07-04.
- Marcus + Observability: create canary dashboard skeleton and perf traces for synthetic spike tests. Due: 2026-07-13.

Notes-to-self / prep talking points
- Start meeting with the customer ask anecdote (Acme / chat automation) — makes tradeoffs concrete.
- Push for concrete owners and dates; avoid "we'll probably" language.
- Watch for "scope creep" from Research: prioritize 50 anchors, not 300.
- Keep latency vs cost trade framed as: "we will not accept >10% tail latency regression without explicit leadership sign-off".

Open questions to resolve in the 1:1
- Is there capacity on infra team for new canary nodes in our West region this quarter? (Marcus to confirm)
- Do we have an automated way to revert cache logic quickly across Dedicated pools? If not, include in rollback plan.
- Who will own the human-annotation batch for anchor prompts? (Research or Solutions Eng?)

Follow-up cadence after this meeting
- Weekly quick sync (15m) until canary launch: Tue 10am (starting 7/14) — attendees: Marcus, Diego, Lena, Uma.
- Decision checkpoint after 2 weeks of canary: leadership readout + go/no-go.

Rough draft blurb for xfunc review (one para)
- "Propose a controlled canary rollout of KV-cache and batching improvements to reduce token-unit costs ~20-30% for common chat workloads. Canary scope: select quantized model variants and 10% hosted traffic. Gating: human-anchored quality checks and p95 latency SLO. Rollback plan and observability will be in place prior to canary start. Requesting alignment and approvals for 6-week spike starting 7/13."

Freeform / brainstorming (not for meeting unless asked)
- Could we experiment with adaptive cache TTLs per-customer to reduce invalidation risk? (needs meta-CRUD policy)
- Consider offering "cost-saver" route toggle in API for customers who choose token-efficiency variants and accept slightly increased tail latency.

End of prep note.

Quick checklist (before 7/06 meeting)
- [ ] Send invites and attach this doc (Uma)
- [ ] Marcus confirms infra capacity (Marcus)
- [ ] Diego prepares a quick eval snapshot (top 10 prompts)
- [ ] Lena prepares 1-slide ask for roadmap review

-- Uma
